title: Guide on How to Setup and Use the HighLevel MCP Server
snippet:
Connect your AI assistant to HighLevel so it can find CRM records and perform supported actions from your instructions. The HighLevel MCP Server, also called the LeadConnector MCP Server, connects through OAuth: sign in, choose the sub-account or sub-accounts to include, and approve the requested permissions.

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It gives AI assistants a standard way to discover and use tools from connected applications. With the HighLevel MCP Server, your assistant can work with supported CRM data and actions without you needing to know the underlying API.
The active catalog includes **more than 600 read, create, update, and delete operations across 38 domains**. The operations available to your connection depend on the OAuth scopes and permissions you approve.
---
## **Before You Connect**
You need access to the HighLevel sub-account or sub-accounts you want to connect and a supported AI client. ChatGPT users can find the official HighLevel plugin in Plugins. Muse and Grok Bot also offer officially listed apps. For custom MCP connections, use the corresponding URL below.
| AI client | Connection method |
|---|---|
| **Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork** | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2` |
| **ChatGPT, Codex, and other compatible OpenAI clients** | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/` |
| **Cursor** | `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/cursor/v2` |
| **Muse** | Connect the official app in Muse; its OAuth endpoint is `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/muse/v2/` |
| **Grok Bot** | Add HighLevel from **Connect apps** |
| **ChatGPT** | Open ChatGPT → Plugins, search for HighLevel, and connect through OAuth. No manual MCP server URL is required. |
These connections use OAuth. During authorization, sign in to LeadConnector, select the available sub-account(s), and approve the requested scopes. All connection options use the current active LeadConnector MCP operation catalog.

### **Codex**
Add the server and start OAuth authorization:
```
codex mcp add leadconnector --url https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/
codex mcp login leadconnector
```
In the **Codex IDE extension**, open the **gear menu → MCP servers → Add server**, choose **Streamable HTTP**, and enter the same URL. Select **Authenticate** when prompted to complete OAuth.

title: HighLevel MCP Server Setup and Configuration Guide
snippet:
The HighLevel MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server provides a secure way for AI agents and MCP-compatible applications to interact with HighLevel tools and services. Using the MCP Server, AI assistants can retrieve records, update data, automate workflows, and execute actions directly inside HighLevel.
The MCP Server supports integrations across multiple HighLevel services, including contacts, conversations, calendars, opportunities, payments, and locations.
**Production MCP Endpoint**
```plaintext
https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/
```
---
## **Key Benefits of HighLevel MCP Server**
The MCP Server helps developers and AI builders create secure, scalable, and AI-powered workflows inside HighLevel.
- **Centralized AI Access:** Connect AI agents to multiple HighLevel services through a single MCP endpoint.
- **Secure Authentication:** Use Private Integration Tokens with scoped permissions for secure access.
- **Natural Language Automation:** Allow AI assistants to execute workflows using conversational prompts.
- **Multi-Service Connectivity:** Access contacts, conversations, opportunities, calendars, payments, and more.
- **MCP-Compatible Flexibility:** Connect with Cursor, Windsurf, OpenAI Playground, Claude-compatible clients, and custom MCP applications.
---
## **Supported MCP Clients**
The HighLevel MCP Server supports MCP-compatible applications that can connect through HTTP.
Supported clients include:
- Cursor
- Windsurf
- OpenAI Playground
- Claude-compatible MCP clients
- Custom MCP-compatible applications

Private Integration Tokens allow MCP-compatible clients to securely authenticate with HighLevel services.
### **How To Create a Token**
1. Log in to HighLevel.
2. Open the desired sub-account/location.
3. Navigate to **Settings**
.
4. Click **Private Integrations**.
5. Select **Create New Integration**.
6. Choose the required scopes.
7. Click **Create Integration**.
8. Copy and securely store the generated token.
---
## **Configure an MCP-Compatible Client**
Adding the MCP endpoint and authentication headers allows your AI client to discover and execute HighLevel MCP tools.
### **Example MCP Configuration**
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "prod-ghl-mcp": { "url": "https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>", "locationId": "<your-location-id>" } } } }
```

The HighLevel MCP Server currently includes tools across multiple HighLevel services.
### **Calendar Tools**
- `calendars_get-calendar-events`

The LeadConnector MCP (Model Context Protocol) server securely connects MCP-compatible AI assistants to your CRM. Based on the scopes you approve, assistants can find records and perform supported read, create, update, and delete actions.
**Choose the URL that matches your AI client: Claude connects at `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2`, ChatGPT, Codex, and other compatible OpenAI clients connect at `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/openai/v2/`, and Cursor connects at `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/cursor/v2`.**
**HighLevel is officially listed in Muse and Grok Bot.** Connect the Muse app or the Grok Bot app.
MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to large language models. The LeadConnector MCP server gives AI assistants a standardized way to work with your LeadConnector data and operations — without you or the model needing to know the internal details of how the underlying APIs work.
LeadConnector MCP connections use **OAuth**. When you connect, your client opens the LeadConnector sign-in and consent flow. You choose the sub-account or sub-accounts the connection can access and approve the requested scopes.

Use the OAuth endpoint listed for your client, or connect an officially listed app. All connections provide access to the current active LeadConnector MCP operation catalog.

- **Cursor:** `https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/cursor/v2` — Set up the MCP connection.
**Officially listed apps:**
- **Muse:** Connect the app in Muse.
- **Grok Bot:** Connect HighLevel from the app catalog.

title: HighLevel VS
snippet:
With the launch of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, HighLevel is unlocking a new level of intelligent automation. It’s the difference between AI that makes suggestions and AI that gets stuff done.
Whether you're running a fast-paced agency or juggling a dozen client pipelines, the MCP Server helps you delegate repetitive, time-consuming tasks to AI agents that can take real action across your HighLevel account, automatically and securely.

The MCP Server changes that. It acts as the automation adapter between AI agents and the HighLevel ecosystem, giving those agents permissioned access to tools like Calendars, Contacts, Pipelines, Conversations and Payments. That means an AI agent can now schedule appointments, follow up with leads, update [CRM](https://www.gohighlevel.com/crm) records, manage pipeline stages and even pull transaction data…without anyone logging in, clicking around or writing a single line of code.

One of the best parts about the MCP Server is that it works with AI tools you already know, like Cursor, Windsurf or OpenAI’s Playground. There’s no need for custom middleware, complex SDKs or developer resources. Just generate a secure token from your HighLevel account, define what your AI can access and go.
**It’s powerful enough for developers, but designed with non-technical users in mind.**

This launch builds on what HighLevel AI already does: helping businesses handle calls and texts, automate outreach, rebook appointments, generate content and even build full websites and automations with Vibe Coding.
The MCP Server takes it to the next level by enabling external agents to securely operate inside your account in real time, adding an entirely new layer of intelligence and efficiency to your workflows.
## And this is just the beginning.
Our MCP Server currently supports 21 tools. But by the end of the year, that number will grow to **over 250**.
You’ll soon be able to automate actions across nearly every area of your business, from marketing to payments to customer service, using nothing more than a few lines of plain language.
Plus, it paves the way for deeper [AskAI integration](https://highlevel.canny.io/changelog/say-hello-to-faster-and-smarter-assistance-with-ask-ai-mcp-server-integration), so your AI assistant can do even more just by chatting with you, voice or text.

title: HighLevel MCP Multi-Account Support for Claude
snippet:
The HighLevel Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables Claude AI assistants to interact directly with your CRM data across multiple sub-accounts. Agencies can now connect once and work seamlessly across any authorized location without reconnecting.

The HighLevel Model Context Protocol (MCP) server is an integration that allows Claude AI assistants to interact directly with your HighLevel CRM data and operations. MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to large language models.
The Anthropic-specific endpoint (`https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2`) provides Claude with a standardized way to query, automate, and orchestrate everything in your HighLevel account through natural language commands — without you or the model needing to know the internal API details.
This endpoint works with Claude.ai, Claude Code (CLI), and Claude Cowork, giving you flexibility across different Claude environments.
2
## Key Benefits
The multi-account MCP endpoint transforms how agencies manage their HighLevel sub-accounts through Claude AI.
**One Connection for Multiple Sub-Accounts** — Agencies connect once and select which sub-accounts to authorize, eliminating the need for separate connections per location.
**Instant Sub-Account Switching** — Work across different locations in the same conversation by simply naming the sub-account in your request.
**Natural Language Automation** — Issue complex commands in plain English without knowing API syntax or operation names.
**Comprehensive Coverage** — Access 625 operations across 40 product domains, filtered by your OAuth permissions.
**Unified Tool Interface** — Six consistent tools handle discovery, inspection, and execution of all operations without overwhelming the model's context.
**Security by Design** — Every request is scoped to one sub-account, authorized against your installation, and executed with short-lived tokens.

title: How to Use the HighLevel MCP Server
snippet:
This article will show you how to leverage the new GoHighLevel MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to empower your AI agents and copilots to access GoHighLevel data and tools seamlessly — all via a secure, standardized HTTP protocol.

The GoHighLevel MCP server is a standardized, secure protocol that allows AI agents to read and write data in GoHighLevel without needing SDKs or deep custom integrations. You can now give agents access to critical tools like Calendar, Contacts, Conversations, Opportunities, and Payments through a single, unified interface.
## Key Benefits of Using the MCP Server
Connecting your AI agents to GoHighLevel has never been easier or safer.
- Standardized Access: Query and update data through a unified protocol.
- Fast Integration: No SDKs required; works with any HTTP-supporting client.
- Secure: Uses private integration tokens (PITs) for granular, permission-based access.
- Scalable: Designed for future expansion to 250+ tools.
- Flexible: Supports popular clients like Cursor, Windsurf, and OpenAI Playground.

| # | Tool | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Get Calendar Events | calendars_get-calendar-events | Get calendar events using userId, groupId, or calendarId. |
| 2 | Get Appointment Notes | calendars_get-appointment-notes | Retrieve notes for a specific appointment. |
| 3 | Get All Tasks | contacts_get-all-tasks | Retrieve all tasks for a contact. |

| 6 | Get Contact | contacts_get-contact | Fetch contact details. |
| 7 | Update Contact | contacts_update-contact | Update a contact. |
| 8 | Upsert Contact | contacts_upsert-contact | Update or create a contact. |
| 9 | Create Contact | contacts_create-contact | Create a new contact. |
| 10 | Get Contacts | contacts_get-contacts | Fetch all contacts. |
| 11 | Search Conversation | conversations_search-conversation | Search/filter/sort conversations. |
| 12 | Get Messages | conversations_get-messages | Retrieve messages by conversation ID. |

"locationId": "<sub-account-id>"
}
}
}
}
